topic.title: Michael Jordan bought the Charlotte team for about $275M and sold at a $3B value while it barely won: owners grow with the league, not the scoreboard

shape.name: The rising tide (a losing asset that still made its owner rich)
shape.beats: hook: the famous owner, the price paid and what went wrong -> promise: so what was it worth at the end? -> how it kept failing on its own terms -> the hidden force that paid every owner anyway -> that force grew -> the turn: the value followed the force, not the results -> payoff: the end value and how many times the price -> loop: which really made them rich?
shape.why: Michael Jordan's Charlotte team barely won yet sold at about 11x his price: the value rode the league's growth. Fits any owner whose asset lost but whose market rose (a sports team, a TV channel, a plot of land).

cta: Winning games or owning the team: which made Jordan richer? Comment
